growing_specifications.description: Premier highland cash crop in Benguet and Mountain Province, producing dense yellow and cream-fleshed tubers on deep volcanic ridges.

category_why.title: Why is Potato classified under Tuber Vegetables (Solanaceae)?
category_why.summary: Solanum tuberosum develops modified swollen underground stem structures (tubers) serving as carbohydrate energy reserves.
points: Underground Stem Tubers: Develops on the tips of stolons, distinct from true root crops like carrots and sweet potatoes.
Solanaceous Characteristics: Compound pinnate foliage and star-shaped flowers typical of the nightshade family.
Highland Photoperiod & Thermal Adaptation: Requires cool night temperatures (15°C–20°C) to trigger tuberization.

harvest_why.title: Why is Potato harvested at 90–105 days following de-haulming?
harvest_why.summary: Vine cutting (de-haulming) 10–14 days prior to harvest allows the tender skin to cure and set, preventing skin feathering and storage rots.
points: Sprouting & Emergence (Days 10–20): Chitted seed tubers produce robust dark green shoots in friable soil ridges.
Stolon & Tuber Initiation (Days 35–50): Flowering coincides with rapid swelling of stolon tips into marble-sized tubers.
Tuber Bulking (Days 50–85): Maximum starch deposition and potassium uptake; requires steady moisture.
De-Haulming (Days 85–95): Cutting vines stops late blight spread and initiates suberization (skin hardening).
Dry Harvest (Days 95–105): Careful digging in dry soil preserves unblemished Grade A tubers.

watering_why.title: Why do Potatoes demand uniform moisture without drought-deluge cycles?
watering_why.summary: Fluctuating moisture triggers internal physiological defects including Hollow Heart and severe tuber splitting.
points: Hollow Heart Prevention: Steady irrigation prevents irregular core expansion and star-shaped internal cavities.
Soft Rot Mitigation: Avoiding waterlogged furrows protects lenticels from asphyxiation and bacterial soft rot.
Pre-Harvest Soil Drydown: Halting irrigation 10 days before digging promotes clean, rot-resistant skins.

soil_why.title: Why do Potatoes thrive in slightly acidic volcanic sandy loam (pH 5.0–6.0)?
soil_why.summary: Acidic pH suppresses Common Scab bacteria while deep friable ridges facilitate unhindered tuber expansion and earthing-up.
points: Common Scab Suppression: Streptomyces scabies thrives at pH > 6.5; acidic soil maintains clean, smooth skin.
Earthing-Up Protection: 20–25 cm ridges shield tubers from sunlight, preventing toxic solanine greening.
Zero Physical Resistance: Stone-free loam prevents deformed, cracked, and misshapen tubers.

varieties.description: Dominant commercial table potato in the Cordillera with smooth yellow skin, deep yellow flesh, high yield, and excellent boiling quality.
High-yielding BPI-BNCRDC release selected for superior tolerance to late blight (Phytophthora infestans) during the monsoon season.
